rated_messages.input_message: Think about a happy memory to ease the difficulty of your urge. Is there something you have been wanting to do for a while that you know you would enjoy? Reading? Walking? Calling a friend? Doing a puzzle? Do something that matters to you instead of smoking.
If leaving social situations to avoid smokers feels awkward, make sure you have something to do instead - take sugar free mints, lollipops or low fat snacks to chew, or use a stress ball.
If you find sounds soothing, tune in to the soundtrack of nature, like crashing waves, the wind rustling through trees, or birds singing.
Don't test yourself needlessly. If this social situation gets uncomfortable then leave briefly if you can. It really helps and it's fine to do it more than once!
If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, try taking the next call in a place where you can't smoke and focus on the conversation. The urge will pass.
Practice going 10 minutes without smoking. Think of it just as practice. When the urge passes, reward yourself with a break from work or dinner from your favorite restaurant!

Think of urges as loud construction noises. Sometimes there's nothing you can do except agree that it's annoying. If you fight it, you feel more irritated, right? Let your urge be there until it passes on its own.
Each time you choose to not smoke after seeing someone else light up, you lessen the habit a little more.

Reduce your stress by using your next break to list four things that have gone well so far today. It might feel like a bit of effort, but doing this will help your mind to refocus, and help you to feel calmer.
You cant always control when you will see other people smoking. But you can control how you respond to your urge when you do.
